incident-bot: [03:12:00 UTC] ALERT: continuous-batch controller detected sustained P99 token latency > 2.5s on pool=shared-usw2. metric: token_latency_p99=3.2s, queue_depth=420, microbatch_evictions=high. auto-notify oncall. https://alerts.redwood/example

mike (oncall): got the page. jumping in. any customer-facing errors?

cs-bot: handful of 502s reported for /v1/generate from customer: AcmePay. rate ~0.5% of requests in last 5m.

mike (oncall): ok. quick hypothesis: continuous batching blowout + KV cache thrash causing extreme queueing. seen similar when microbatch sizes spike under high concurrency.

lee: I’m seeing controller logs with repeated `microbatch_commit` delays and >50% failed KV cache lookups. snippet: ```
[03:11:58] controller: enqueue req id=abcd shard=12
[03:12:02] runtime: kvcache miss id=abcd key=ctx-xx evict=true
[03:12:03] controller: microbatch assemble delayed 3200ms
```

pranav: any rollout or autoscale change in last 30m?

mike (oncall): deployment history: no model changes. autoscaler spike ~03:09 added 3 pods then oscillated. config shows `max_microbatch_size` defaulted to 16 for this model. suspect large tails + jitter.

lee: can we fast limit microbatch size + enable stricter batching timeouts to drain queue? propose: set max_microbatch_size=4 and batch_timeout_ms=25 in controller for pool=shared-usw2.

mike (oncall): +1. Also cap concurrent incoming requests per-shard to reduce queueing: `concurrency_per_shard=48`.

pranav: preparing hotpatch. command I’ll run: ```sh
redwoodctl patch controller shared-usw2 
  --set max_microbatch_size=4 
  --set batch_timeout_ms=25 
  --set concurrency_per_shard=48
```

mike (oncall): run it. include `--dry-run` first? low risk but this needs immediate mitigation.

pranav: doing live apply now (no dry-run) to avoid delay. applying to 50% of pods first, 30s pause.

incident-bot: [03:18:12 UTC] change applied to controller/shared-usw2 (canary) -> max_microbatch_size=4, batch_timeout_ms=25, concurrency_per_shard=48

lee: canary logs look better: microbatch assemble delay down to ~120ms, queue_depth on canary pods dropped 70%.

mike (oncall): good. start ramp to 100% if stable for 60s. watch p99 and kvcache evictions.

pranav: ramping to 100% now.

incident-bot: [03:20:05 UTC] rollout 100% complete.

cs-bot: AcmePay 502s rate reduced to ~0.02% in last 2m. They reported improvement via support.

lee: still seeing periodic KV cache spike events on a minority of shards—likely a cascade from earlier eviction storms. I’ll trigger a targeted KVcache warmup on those shards: `kvtool preheat --shard 12,18 --prefix-size=128`

mike (oncall): good idea. also enable temporary fallback policy for heavy requests: route requests > 8k tokens to model=xlarge-compat (less batching) to avoid re-trigger. small config: ```json
{ "route_policy": "heavy_req_fallback", "token_threshold": 8000, "fallback_model": "xlarge-compat" }
```

pranav: applied fallback route.

lee: after warmup, eviction rate down to baseline. overall token p99 at 420ms now.

mike (oncall): customer impact mitigated. opening post-incident note. who wants to own follow-up RCA and a permanent controller limit?

pranav: I can drive RCA. plan: correlate request size distribution + microbatch assembly times, see if a smarter adaptive microbatch cap per-model prevents this.

lee: will capture KV cache metrics and propose improved eviction thresholds. also think we should add a controller circuit-breaker to prevent controller-wide microbatch size increases during eviction storms.

mike (oncall): nice. I'll update SLAs and notify support to close customer tickets. handing off to @pranav for post-mortem. I’m removing myself from live paging.

pranav: taking over at 03:56 UTC. notes: mitigations = microbatch cap, batch timeout, concurrency cap, kv warmup, heavy-request fallback. next steps: RCA doc, config guardrails, canary tests for batch controller changes.

mike (oncall): ack. thanks team :thumbsup:

pranav: leaving a short checklist for next oncall:
- monitor token_latency_p99 and queue_depth alerts
- watch KVcache_eviction_rate > 5/min -> throttle ingress
- verify fallback route health

incident-bot: [03:56:40 UTC] HANDOFF: oncall=mike -> oncall=pranav

pranav: tagging product + SRE for follow-up. closing thread for live mitigation; keeping thread open for RCA comments.
